inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: FY2026 weighted average diluted EPS denominator 358,985,138 (Annual FY2026 line 6535); basic 357.2m. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report segment note / below-EBITDA table (line 1992): share-based payments A$29.3m (FY2025 A$19.5m). FY2026 is inflated by a one-off executive rights grant and employee share grant. No separate equity-award withholding-tax line is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0).
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built: 10-year Commonwealth bond ~4.4% + 5.5% ERP x beta ~1.1 gives cost of equity ~10.5%; ~20% debt at ~6% pre-tax (4.2% post-tax) gives ~9.2%, rounded to 9.0%. One WACC for all three scenarios: AI-disruption and cycle risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B (leases as operating cost). Lease cash cost = A$13.9m principal + A$6.5m interest = A$20.4m (1.7% of net revenue) deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities of A$170.4m are EXCLUDED from net debt; D&A is ex right-of-use depreciation (A$162.0m total less A$16.3m ROU = A$145.7m, 12.2% of net revenue).
inputs.interest_income_treatment: Not stripped: SEEK is a net-debt company (A$962.4m) and the flows are unlevered (built from EBITDA), so the A$4.4m of interest received never enters them.
inputs.revenue_basis: base_revenue is NET revenue (A$1,198.9m: ANZ 945.4 + Asia 253.5), the basis of the segment EBITDA table and of management's margin commentary. The Metrics CSV carries gross sales revenue of A$1,284.2m for FY2026, which grosses up Sidekicker contingent-labour pass-through costs acquired in H2 FY2025; EBITDA of A$529.9m is 44.2% of net and 41.3% of gross revenue. All percent paths here are on net revenue.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating marketplace; routing row 'Operating company: marketplaces', with the non-US adaptations for AUD WACC, leases and non-operating assets). FRESH BUILD - no prior valuation, no memory entry. Continuing operations only: Zhaopin (deconsolidated FY2021) and Latin America are out of the flows; statutory FY2026 net loss of A$371.3m is driven by a A$283.6m Zhaopin impairment, a A$72.4m receivable impairment and a A$269.2m Growth Fund mark-down, none of which touch operating cash flow. Sum-of-parts element: the equity-accounted SEEK Growth Fund and Zhaopin stake produce no income in the flows and are added through equity_bridge at haircut carrying value (matching-asset rule). Growth Fund management fees (A$20.0m) and capital calls (A$34.0m in FY2026) sit in investing cash flow, outside both EBITDA and reported FCF; they are covered by the 25% haircut on the Fund rather than charged in the flows. Buybacks: none (buyback_cash 0); basic count has drifted only 353.1m to 357.2m over five years, so the flat count is close to what the company actually delivers. NO FY2027 GUIDANCE WAS AVAILABLE: the folder holds the FY2026 annual report but not the August 2026 results presentation, and the annual report states only that productivity savings are 'included in the FY2027 budget and guidance'. Year-1 drivers are therefore judgment from FY2026 run-rates, not guidance; replace them when the presentation is added. The qualitative Analysis JSON was not on disk at build time, so scenario axes are drawn from the FY2026 annual report directly. The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range (10.86-25.77) after a de-rating the Chairman/CEO letter attributes to AI uncertainty.

equity_bridge.item: SEEK Growth Fund, after tax and 25% haircut
equity_bridge.note: Equity-accounted carrying A$1,503.1m (FY2026 AR balance sheet review, line 2142) less deferred tax liability on SEEK's future interest in the Fund A$183.6m (Note 6(c)(i)) = A$1,319.5m, x 0.75. Haircut covers Level-3 marks on unlisted HR SaaS / online education assets (the Fund was marked down 13% in FY2026), illiquidity, and the ~A$20m/yr management fee plus carried interest that are not charged in the flows.

equity_bridge.note: Carrying A$172.3m (approximately the expected simplification-transaction price, Note 21) + net receivable A$7.7m (Note 10(iii)) = A$180.0m, x 0.70. No binding agreement at 30 June 2026; China macro and counterparty risk.

equity_bridge.note: A$12.1m performance fee to the Fund Manager (paid August 2026) + A$29.4m statutory interest on a historical transaction (Note 15)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: yield-led net revenue growth (FY2026 net revenue +10% on flat-to-down volumes), decelerating; equity CAGR rejected as an anchor
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is unusable as the growth anchor: book value is dominated by non-operating marks (FY2021 Zhaopin sell-down gain, FY2023 Growth Fund deconsolidation gain, FY2024 and FY2026 Zhaopin impairments, FY2026 Fund mark-down) and diverges from revenue by far more than 30%. EPS CAGRs are not meaningful (FY2026 statutory EPS -1.039, continuing -0.858, both impairment-driven; FY2021 and FY2023 include discontinued-operations gains).
historical_growth.notes: Revenue is the CSV series (continuing operations from FY2021): FY2021 760.3, FY2023 1,225.3, FY2026 1,284.2. The 5-year figure starts from the FY2021 COVID trough and the 3-year figure from the FY2023 post-COVID hiring peak, and FY2026 gross revenue includes Sidekicker pass-through; neither is a clean run-rate. FCF CAGRs are on owner FCF (reported continuing FCF less SBC; no interest-income strip because the company is in net debt): FY2021 65.1, FY2023 117.0, FY2026 216.7. Both start from depressed bases (FY2021 trough; FY2023 peak Platform Unification capex of A$189.4m) and overstate sustainable growth. SBC grew from A$18.8m to A$29.3m over three years (one-off grants in FY2026), slower than FCF, so the owner-FCF CAGR is not being flattered by stock pay.

base.rationale: FY0 anchors on net revenue: EBITDA margin 44.2% (FY2025 42.1%), SBC 2.4% (1.8% in FY2025 before one-off grants), D&A ex-ROU 12.2%, capex 12.7%, adjusted effective tax rate 27.8% (29.0% in FY2025; R&D incentive credits). Working capital set to zero: unearned income fell A$183.0m to A$170.0m while revenue grew, and FY2026 cash conversion of 104% was supplier-payment timing.

scenario_narratives.base: Yield keeps doing the work. FY2026 was the sixth straight year of double-digit yield growth (ANZ +14%, Asia paid +20%) from depth-product adoption and value-based pricing, against ANZ volumes of -1% and Asia paid volumes of -12% as freemium rolls out. Base assumes yield growth fades from the mid-teens to mid-single digits as tier upgrades saturate, volumes stabilise near today's cyclically soft level without a sharp rebound, and placement share holds. Net revenue grows 7% fading to 3%. Operating leverage (four consecutive halves; costs +8% against revenue +10% in FY2026) lifts EBITDA margin from 44.2% to 48%, and capex intensity eases from 12.7% to 10.5% of revenue as Platform Unification spend rolls off into amortisation while AI compute partly replaces it.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI turns out to reinforce the incumbent: SEEK's live data, matching and verification let it price on placement outcomes, so yield compounds in the low double digits for several more years at the same time as Australian job-ad volumes recover from a multi-year decline and Asia's freemium funnel converts free hirers to paid. Net revenue grows 10-11% for three years and EBITDA margin reaches 52%, a level consistent with dominant classified marketplaces, on a unified platform that needs less capital. Requires volume recovery and sustained pricing power together.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI disintermediates the paid job ad. Agentic sourcing tools, LinkedIn and large-employer direct hiring take candidate matching away from the listing, hirers push back on six years of price increases once applicant quality can be had elsewhere, and paid volumes fall structurally rather than cyclically; Asia freemium fails to monetise. Net revenue peaks in FY2027 and falls about 16% over the following six years. SEEK has to keep spending on product and AI compute to defend share, so costs do not fall with revenue: EBITDA margin compresses from 44% to 35% and capex stays at 12%+ of revenue. Leverage of 1.8x net debt/EBITDA rises but stays serviceable; this is an erosion case, not a solvency case, and the terminal value does not hit the zero floor.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved off the 15/50/35 house default to a symmetric 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: AI-driven disintermediation of paid job ads is a structural, not cyclical, threat that cannot yet be tested against evidence either way, and the share price has roughly halved from its 52-week high on exactly this fear. Base 50%: it extends a six-year yield record and four halves of operating leverage at a decelerating rate. Bull cut to 25%: it needs a volume recovery and continued double-digit pricing power at the same time, two independent things going right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: SEEK is valued as two pieces: the APAC employment marketplace on an unlevered owner-FCF DCF (SBC expensed, leases as an operating cost, flat diluted share count), plus its passive investments (SEEK Growth Fund, Zhaopin) at haircut after-tax carrying value through the equity bridge. The marketplace is a dominant, high-margin, capital-light classifieds business whose value turns on whether AI strengthens or bypasses the paid listing; that question is carried in the three scenario paths rather than in the discount rate. Roughly A$3 per share of every scenario's value is the investment portfolio, which is marked to Level-3 valuations and is identical across scenarios.
key_risks_to_valuation: No FY2027 guidance was available in the folder (results presentation missing); year-1 growth and margin are judgment from FY2026 run-rates
AI disintermediation of paid job ads (the bear case) - structural, with no historical precedent to calibrate against
Yield growth has carried revenue for six years against falling volumes; the model assumes it fades gradually rather than reverses
SEEK Growth Fund carrying value (A$1,503m, Level-3, marked down 13% in FY2026) is about 19% of base equity value even after tax and a 25% haircut, and is not scenario-dependent in this build
Zhaopin simplification transaction is non-binding; the A$172.3m carrying value rests on an expected transaction price
Capitalised development spend is about 12% of revenue; if AI investment keeps capex above amortisation, the terminal margin is overstated
Net debt of A$962m (1.8x EBITDA) amplifies equity value changes in the bear path
